selection_note: Cases are explanatory examples chosen after viewing D evidence, not independent confirmation, nor an extra gate. Two fixed candidates were appended only after the parent froze full-IS selection. No new candidate search or OOS access was performed.
clock: Signal-close prices and already-earned BASE PnL; macro observation strictly earlier than signal and no older than seven calendar days. Original entry fills next quote close.

cases.title: USD-direction conflict together with an adverse directional rate spread
cases.hypothesis_not_causal_claim: Joint losses are present in both halves while A-only and B-only are profitable in both. The combined D single-state A/B totals are positive, so this is a descriptive example of a joint loss pocket hidden by single-state aggregation. The price-only PnL does not credit carry; the explanation is a hypothesis about market context, not financing or causation.

cases.title: Moderate-low path efficiency with slightly contracting short-horizon volatility
cases.hypothesis_not_causal_claim: The joint cohort has worse expectancy than A-only and B-only in both halves. B-only is already losing in both halves, so this refines an existing single-state weakness rather than proving that the single-state view missed all losses. The D2 payoff ratio of the joint exceeds A-only/B-only despite lower win rate; exclusion need not improve every metric.

cases.title: Strong recent directional move inside a low-efficiency 63-quote path
cases.hypothesis_not_causal_claim: A strong recent move may be an oscillation within a choppy longer path. Joint expectancy is below A-only/B-only in both halves, but B-only also loses; this is a conditional severity distinction. Both halves have modest samples and later performance is unexamined in this explanatory analysis.

cases.title: Low long-path efficiency with mild positive directional 20-quote return
cases.hypothesis_not_causal_claim: Added after the parent froze the original full-IS screen result. This case only describes the fixed D state and does not change its parameters, selection or thresholds. A direction-aligned but sub-one-volatility move may be a weak vote on a noisy 63-quote path; causation is unproved.

cases.title: Low long-path efficiency with mild opposite directional 20-quote return
cases.hypothesis_not_causal_claim: Added after the parent froze the original full-IS screen result. This case only describes the fixed D state. A modest counter-direction move on a noisy long path can be consistent with weak mean-reversion evidence, but the observed conditional outcomes do not establish causation.

counterexamples.fact: D1/D2 joint n=41/37 and negative sums, but B-only n=0 in both halves and D. The joint rejected-episode set equals B alone throughout D, so this is not extra interaction information.

No efficiency state 0/1 ? volatility-ratio state 3 cell satisfies D1 and D2 n>=10 and negative sums plus combined D negative. No efficiency state 2/3 ? directional-return state 0 cell satisfies those conditions either. This does not prove those mechanisms absent; the predeclared sample/repetition condition is unmet.

overlap_diagnostics.scope: Equality/Jaccard computed from original D trade IDs within an account. D1/D2/D overlap, different accounts share market shocks, and D-only equality need not persist later. Future path-equivalence diagnostics must use exact original signal IDs/accepted masks, preserve all passing versions, and remain diagnostic.

interpretation_limits: No p-values, causal effect or expected OOS profitability is claimed.
The 267 cells reuse previously observed IS and share trades; they are not independent experiments.
UNKNOWN is a separate retained partition, never implicitly rejected. A_all/B_all include opposite-feature UNKNOWN and can overlap UNKNOWN partition.
All reported PnL is the sum of original complete BASE trade returns, fixed-principal percentage points with zero cost; no filtered daily curve has been simulated by this probe.
Efficiency uses absolute 63-quote net price change divided by sum of absolute daily price changes; directional return20 is divided by realized_vol20*sqrt(20/252).
DXY contains some studied currencies, so its relation to individual FX is partly structural; directional interest spread is context only and no carry is credited.
D totals can differ from D1+D2 due to trades crossing the 2009/2010 boundary.
